title: Olfactory differences among cactophilic Drosophila species.
abstract: Divergence of behavioral traits with adaptation to changes in the environment has been well documented in many animals and is often accompanied by divergence in sensory systems. Shifts in insect host plant preference behavior, in particular, are often associated with changes to the olfactory system, including differences in the sensitivity, specificity, or abundance of olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs). Here, we examine 12 species from the cactophilic Drosophila repleta group that represent three broad host-use categories: Opuntia specialists, columnar cactus specialists, and polymorphic species that use both host types. We recorded odor-evoked responses from all six maxillary palp OSN classes using single sensillum recordings and used electropalpograms to further evaluate species in which a pb2B-like class was not detected by single sensillum recordings (SSRs). The B-neuron classes clustered largely by OSN identity across species, retaining characteristic class-specific response profiles. The A-neuron classes were less clearly separated because of weak or overlapping response profiles. Despite these shared class-specific responses, species differed substantially in response magnitude and sensitivity to odorants. A pb2B-like class was not detected by SSR in D. mulleri, D. aldrichi, and D. straubae. Electropalpograms supported the absence or strong reduction of a phenol-responsive palpal signal in D. mulleri and D. straubae, while D. aldrichi retained a strong response. Principal component and phylogenetic principal component analyses did not reveal consistent clustering by host-use category. These results suggest that maxillary palp olfaction has evolved in a species- or lineage-specific manner rather than through a repeated host-category-specific shift in peripheral sensitivity.

title: Microbial products trigger chemosensory dialogues through intestinal G protein-coupled receptors.
abstract: Organismal reactions to changing environmental conditions require information relays that sense cues and elicit appropriate responses. G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including olfactory receptors, comprise the largest receptor family that recognizes environmental cues, consisting of over 800 genes in the human genome. Here, by screening libraries of gut metabolites and natural products using a multiplexed GPCR reporter system, GPCR-seq, we reveal multiple intestinal chemosensory pathways. Among these, we determine that a cyclic fatty acid promotes serotonin production from enterochromaffin cells via olfactory receptor OR51E1. Two additional gut microbe-derived molecules, a β-carboline and 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), function as agonists for GPR35, a receptor linked to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The IBD-associated GPR35 risk variant, T108M, shows aberrant responses to 6-HNA, while Enterocloster bolteae, a species increased in IBD, generates high levels of 6-HNA. This approach provides an accelerated path to mapping critical chemosensory pathways and host physiological responses.

title: Multidimensional characterization of vegetable breads using multisource intelligent sensory technologies and feature-level data fusion.
abstract: Food sensory quality is multidimensional, and a single intelligent sensory technique cannot simultaneously characterize color, taste, and odor across multiple dimensions. Multisource intelligent sensory analysis combined with data fusion provides an approach for the objective characterization of multidimensional food sensory characteristics. Control bread (CK) and four vegetable breads prepared with pumpkin (PU), The vegetable juices produced distinct color, taste-response, and volatile-compound characteristics in the breads. The first three electronic-eye principal components explained 91.95% of the variance. PU was dominated by strong yellow and vivid yellow, RP showed a clear orange-yellow appearance, and CE retained a green hue. The first two electronic-tongue principal components explained 90.03% of the variance. PG showed relatively high umami and bitterness response indices, whereas CE showed a relatively high saltiness response index. The first five principal components of the electronic-nose data explained 82.89% of the variance, and 17 volatile compounds were tentatively assigned. PG showed high responses for several fermentation-related volatiles. A peak tentatively assigned to acetone was detected only in RP under the current analytical conditions, whereas peaks tentatively assigned to myrcene and β-phellandrene showed pronounced responses in CE. After feature-level data fusion, the first three principal components explained 80.78% of the variance. Loading analysis showed that multiple latent variables from the electronic eye, electronic tongue, and electronic nose jointly contributed to the multidimensional characterization of the formulations. Breads prepared with different vegetable juices exhibited distinct characteristics in terms of color, taste-response profiles, and volatile-compound profiles. Feature-level fusion of multisource intelligent sensory data enables the joint representation of information from these three instrumental dimensions within a unified analytical framework, providing a methodological framework for the multidimensional characterization of vegetable breads.

title: Three-dimensional nanogap substrate for metal-enhanced fluorescence-based ultra-sensitive detection of trace ammonia.
abstract: High sensitivity and rapid detection of trace ammonia are crucial for environmental monitoring and disease diagnosis. Polydiacetylene (PDA)-based sensors have attracted significant attention due to their fast response; however, weak fluorescence signals under low ammonia concentrations limit their performance. To address this issue, this study further developed a PDA-based ammonia sensing platform based on a three-dimensional (3D) silver nanogap substrate by utilizing the metal-enhanced fluorescence (MEF) effect to enhance the fluorescence response of PDA. Specifically, a nanopillar array with a diameter of 250 nm, a height of 100 nm, and a period of 500 nm was fabricated on a glass slide using ultraviolet nanoimprint lithography. After that, an oxygen plasma treatment was applied to form a nanogap network, and a 75 nm thick silver layer was deposited on the surface via physical vapor deposition (PVD) to create a 3D silver nanogap structure, thus constructing the 3D nanogap substrate. Following this, PDA vesicles were then immobilized on the substrate surface for ammonia sensing. Experimental results demonstrated that, under static sealed-chamber conditions, the 3D nanogap substrate achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 4.79 ppm for ammonia, calculated using the standard 3σ/k method based on the theoretically estimated ammonia concentration. In addition, the sensor exhibited excellent selectivity toward ammonia compared with volatile organic compounds such as toluene, ethanol, and methanol, demonstrating great potential for trace ammonia detection applications.

title: Exploratory whole-genome sequencing of cagA-positive Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric biopsies: descriptive observations in COL3A1, ICAM1, and COLEC12.
abstract: Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric disease involves sustained inflammation, stromal responses, and extracellular-matrix remodeling, yet genomic observations shared across different clinical categories remain poorly defined. This study aimed to describe variant-associated gene annotations in four cagA-positive gastric-biopsy specimens with different documented clinical and histological findings, without inferring within-patient progression. Whole-genome sequencing (2 × 151 bp; approximately 37.7× mean mappable depth) was performed on gastric-biopsy DNA from four unrelated adults with active gastritis, normal histology with positive H. pylori screening assays, gastric ulcer, and intestinal-type adenocarcinoma. Variant-associated gene sets were annotated by KEGG, Reactome, and Gene Ontology over-representation analysis with within-analysis Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction, and term-level outputs were examined for denominator consistency, gene-family representation, and overlapping membership. Across six analysis sets and five annotation collections, 141 BH-significant term occurrences represented 94 distinct database-term pairs. The intersection of significant-term contributors from three principal analysis sets contained 133 genes, including 124 olfactory-receptor genes and nine other genes. COL3A1, ICAM1, and COLEC12 were examined as literature-informed discussion targets. Five of six displayed alleles had global gnomAD-genome frequencies above 20%, whereas ICAM1 rs542476616 was rare globally. No category association was tested. The study describes shared genomic annotations in four cagA-positive gastric biopsies and provides a traceable term-level analysis. COL3A1, ICAM1, and COLEC12 motivate further genotype-confirmed and clinically adjudicated investigation; their recurrence does not establish diagnostic performance or a disease-associated variant effect.

title: Disentangling Response Magnitude and Relative MOS Sensor Fingerprints for Electronic-Nose Screening of Off-Odor in Table Olives.
abstract: A multichannel metal-oxide semiconductor (MOS) electronic-nose response contains complementary information on overall response magnitude and the relative pattern among sensors. The most appropriate representation therefore depends on whether the aim is to distinguish volatile profiles, response levels, or both. This study compared three mathematically linked representations of the same six-channel NASYS S3+ response: global magnitude (M), centered log-ratio profiles (CLR), and per-sensor log-conductance ratios (LGR), which retain both components. Reference solutions varied both compound identity and concentration (four compounds, three levels, six sessions). The same framework was applied to 24 commercial cans of Californian-style black table olives preassigned by the supplier as conforming (C), mild (DS), or strong (DF) barnyard-like off-odor: 15 for calibration, six reserved before fitting, and three coded unknowns. Using the same linear discriminant analysis (LDA), CLR retained reference-compound class information better than M (balanced accuracy, BA, 0.83-0.89 vs. ≤0.56). In olives, grouped cross-validation favored M (BA 0.900), whereas LGR classified all six reserve cans and M only four; both results are descriptive within-campaign comparisons on 15 and 6 cans, not external validation. The three coded unknowns matched the concealed supplier labels. Signal representation should therefore be selected according to the analytical question rather than solely by calibration cross-validation performance.

title: Similar degenerative patterns of olfactory receptor genes in the giant panda and marine carnivores.
abstract: Olfactory receptor (OR) genes constitute the largest mammalian gene family and are critical for olfactory perception and ecological adaptation. OR gene variation is associated with interspecific differences in habitat, diet, and sensory reliance, yet the relative contributions of these ecological factors to OR evolution remain unclear. Here, we systematically analyzed OR repertoires across 25 carnivoran species occupying diverse niches. Marine carnivorans exhibit convergent OR degeneration, with fewer intact genes and ancestral orthologs, higher pseudogene ratios, and relaxed purifying selection compared with terrestrial species. Notably, bamboo-specialized giant pandas display identical degenerative signatures, possessing the smallest intact OR repertoire and most lost ancestral OR groups among terrestrial carnivorans. Our models show habitat primarily shapes intact OR quantity, while dietary specialization governs pseudogenization and selective constraints. These findings reveal convergent OR functional decay under aquatic adaptation and extreme dietary specialization, illustrating complex links between lifestyle and chemosensory genome evolution in mammals.

title: Colony isolation of odorant receptor-expressing insect sensor cells in hollow hydrogel microparticles for enhanced biohybrid sensor sensitivity.
abstract: Cell-based biohybrid sensors using insect olfactory receptors (ORs) have emerged as promising sensing platforms for the selective and sensitive detection of biomarkers. A single sensor cell provides a weak signal, so the readout of most biohybrid sensors is the accumulated response of a whole population of cells. Response heterogeneity within engineered sensor cell populations can limit sensor sensitivity because low-responding cells dilute the bulk-averaged signal. Selecting highly responsive subclones could improve sensor sensitivity. However, most insect cell lines proliferate poorly at low cell density, making it challenging to obtain expandable colonies from a single insect cell. Here, we present a colony-isolation workflow for insect sensor cells using hollow hydrogel microparticles (PicoShells). Insect sensor cells were encapsulated in PicoShells at limiting dilutions to physically isolate one or a few cells. The encapsulated insect sensor cells were co-cultured with non-encapsulated support cells in the same suspension culture to promote colony formation. Individual colony-containing PicoShells were isolated and expanded into subclonal cell lines. Functional screening using a portable fluorescence detector and a microwell array identified a highly responsive subclone. In a human urine sample spiked with acetophenone, a candidate volatile biomarker of disease, this subclone showed an approximately 2.4-fold higher response sensitivity than the parental cell line, and the limit of detection was reduced from 1.56 ± 0.17 μM to 0.93 ± 0.22 μM for this subclone. These results indicate that colony isolation using PicoShells, combined with functional screening, provides a practical strategy for improving the sensitivity of insect cell biohybrid sensors.

title: Insights into the flavor evolution of braised chicken during six-month storage via sensory evaluation, E-tongue, E-nose, and GC-IMS.
abstract: The flavor of braised chicken tends to deteriorate during prolonged storage. This study systematically investigated dynamic changes in the flavor of braised chicken during six-month storage. Sensory and physicochemical analyses revealed a relatively stable appearance and color, but a noticeable deterioration in taste and texture. Odor degraded most significantly. The electronic tongue (E-tongue) detected a taste shift toward decreased umami and richness and increased saltiness. The electronic nose (E-nose) supported the dominant role of odor by revealing a substantial build-up of sulfur- and nitrogen-containing volatiles. Gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry analysis identified 67 volatile compounds in braised chicken during storage. Orthogonal partial least squares-discriminant analysis screening identified ten key differential compounds. Among these, octanal, diethyl disulfide, butanoic acid, and 2-furanmethanethiol showed strong correlations with sensory deterioration and served as potential markers of flavor degradation. This study provides a reference for evaluating the edibility and salability of braised chicken during its shelf-life.

title: Decoding the Dynamic Evolution and Metabolic Pathways of Volatile and Non-Volatile Flavors in Prepared Fish Fillets during Boiling: An Integrated Approach of HS-SPME-GC-MS, HS-GC-IMS, E-Nose, and Chemometrics.
abstract: This study examined how boiling time (0-150 s) affects the flavor of prepared grass carp fillets. Using headspace solid-phase microextraction gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS) and headspace gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (HS-GC-IMS), we identified 146 volatile organic compounds (VOCs), of which 15 were defined as key odorants. Shorter boiling (30-60 s) enhanced the release of volatiles like 1-octen-3-ol and (Z)-4-heptenal, imparting mushroom and fruity notes. The 90 s stage featured nutty and oily aromas from compounds such as 2,5-dimethyl-3-isopropylpyrazine and heptanal. Extended boiling (120-150 s) led to the dominance of sweet and grassy notes from isoeugenol and propionaldehyde. The core free amino acids (FAAs)─aspartic acid (Asp), glutamic acid (Glu), and histidine (His)─shaped the primary taste profile, and VOC formation was closely linked to amino acid and nucleotide metabolism. This work provides a theoretical basis for optimizing the flavor quality of prepared fish products.

title: Dynamic aroma evolution of peach juice during thermal processing: Integrating volatilomics and non-volatile metabolomics to elucidate precursor-aroma relationships.
abstract: Flavor quality is a critical determinant of consumer acceptance of peach juice (PJ). However, the dynamic evolution of aroma compounds and their relationships with non-volatile precursors during thermal processing remains insufficiently understood. This study employed an integrated analytical strategy combining quantitative descriptive analysis (QDA), electronic nose, HS-SPME-GC/MS-based volatilomics, and non-targeted metabolomics to systematically elucidate aroma evolution and its associations with non-volatile metabolites in PJs subjected to thermal processing. Sensory evaluation and volatile analysis revealed a clear stage-dependent and dynamic aroma trajectory, in which moderate heating significantly enhanced desirable peach-like, floral, sweet, and creamy notes, while excessive heating induced off-flavors. Notably, the 12-min treatment (PJ4) exhibited the most favorable aroma profile among the tested treatments while satisfying commercial sterility requirements. Totally 59 volatiles were identified, and combined with GC-O/AI and odor activity values (OAV), 10 key aroma-active compounds, involving γ- and δ-lactones, linalool, and β-ionone, were recognized as key contributors to aroma quality during the mid-heating stage. Metabolomics revealed 1150 non-volatile metabolites following a three-stage dynamic pattern. Integrated KEGG and correlation analyses indicated stage-dependent shifts in metabolites annotated to lipid-, amino acid-, and carbohydrate-related pathways, which were associated with changes in potential aroma precursor pools and aroma-active compounds. These findings provide mechanistic insights into aroma evolution during thermal processing and a basis for further evaluation of flavor optimization strategies in peach juice processing.

title: Non-targeted metabolomics technology elucidates the metabolic mechanism of flavor formation in Xinjiang's distinctive apricot (Prunus armeniaca L.) varieties.
abstract: Apricot is widely popular due to their unique flavor characteristics. This study employs techniques such as the electronic nose (E-nose), electronic tongue (E-tongue), headspace solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC/MS), and ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with electrospray ionization quadrupole-Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UPLC-ESI-Q-Orbitrap-MS) to characterize the flavor compounds of five apricot varieties from the Xinjiang region. The results indicate that Baren apricot (BRX) received the highest scores in sensory evaluation, and its total polyphenol and total flavonoid contents were second only to those of Xiaobai apricot (XBX). E-nose analysis revealed that BRX contains a relatively high abundance of aromatic compounds sensitive to sensors W1C, W3C, and W5C. E-tongue analysis demonstrated that BRX possesses the most superior taste characteristics. Metabolomic analysis of volatile and non-volatile metabolites revealed that a total of 54 volatile organic compounds (VOCs) were detected in BRX, with concentrations significantly higher than those in XBX, Mangguo apricot (MGX), and Shushanggan apricot (SSGX). Orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) further indicated that the content of non-volatile metabolites in BRX consistently exceeded that of the other four apricot varieties. Using BRX as a reference, a total of 22 core flavor compounds were identified, including four VOCs and 18 non-volatile metabolites. The associated metabolic pathways were primarily enriched in carbohydrate metabolism, amino acid degradation, lipid biosynthesis, and secondary metabolism. These findings provide insights into the potential mechanisms underlying the superior flavor quality of BRX and offer a theoretical basis for apricot cultivar selection, breeding, and deep-processing applications.

title: Engineering hydrogel-in-oleogel bigels for reduced-fat and egg-free mayonnaise: relating phase architecture to functional performance.
abstract: Hydrogel-in-oleogel (HG-in-OG) bigels have attracted increasing interest as structured lipid systems for fat replacement, yet the relationships between their phase architecture and functionality in complex foods remain insufficiently understood. In this study, food-grade HG-in-OG bigels were prepared by combining phytosterol/γ-oryzanol oleogels with sodium alginate hydrogels at oleogel fractions ranging from 40% to 80%. Increasing the oleogel fraction progressively refined the dispersed hydrogel domains from 4.21 ± 1.57 μm to 1.77 ± 0.69 μm, accompanied by enhanced network rigidity, reduced molecular mobility, and reduced structural recovery after shear, while interfacial properties changed only marginally. The optimized bigels were subsequently incorporated into bigel-based mayonnaise with egg yolk (BGYM) and bigel-based yolk-free mayonnaise (BGYFM) to investigate the relationship between bigel phase architecture and mayonnaise functionality. All mayonnaise samples remained physically stable during 14 d of storage at 25 °C and exhibited gel-like viscoelastic behavior. Increasing the oleogel fraction markedly reduced the hardness of BGYFM from 1.15 N to 0.26 N, producing textural properties closer to commercial mayonnaise. Although the electronic nose differentiated the aroma profiles of the BG-based mayonnaise formulations, sensory odor responses were less pronounced, whereas overall acceptability varied with mayonnaise type and oleogel fraction. Among the tested formulations, 50BGYM and 60BGYM achieved the highest overall sensory score (7.85). Systematic variation of oleogel fraction was accompanied by coordinated changes in phase architecture, bulk material properties, and mayonnaise functionality, providing a structural basis for the rational design of potentially healthier structured lipid systems.

title: Influence of different cell wall disruption methods on flavor quality of yeast extract: mechanistic insights through peptidomics and molecular docking.
abstract: Yeast extract (YE) is a widely used natural flavor enhancer whose taste and aroma quality govern its industrial value. However, how the cell wall disruption method, the first and decisive step of YE production, shapes flavor at the molecular level remains unclear, leaving method selection largely empirical. In this study, five representative disruption methods, autolysis (AY), ethyl acetate chemical disruption (EA), high-pressure homogenization (HPH), low-temperature colloid milling (LCM), and glucanase enzymatic hydrolysis (GE), were systematically compared using sensory evaluation, electronic nose and tongue, free amino acid and nucleotide profiling, solvent-assisted flavor evaporation coupled with gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (SAFE-GC-O-MS), electroencephalography (EEG), liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) peptidomics, and molecular docking. Results showed that GE produced the highest umami amino acid content (113.01 mg/g DW, p < 0.05) and the lowest bitterness, whereas EA yielded the highest bitter amino acid proportion; SAFE-GC-O-MS identified 117 volatile compounds, of which 67 (odor activity value ≥1) drove inter-group differentiation, and peptidomics revealed 1785 differential peptides, with GE generating more glutamate/aspartate-rich umami-associated peptides. In addition, molecular docking demonstrated that GE-derived acidic peptides bound the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3 most strongly (ΔG down to -9.18 kcal/mol), whereas EA-derived hydrophobic peptides preferentially engaged the bitter receptors TAS2R13/TAS2R14; synthesized-peptide validation corroborated these predictions (r = 0.93). Therefore, entropy-weighted TOPSIS confirmed the ranking GE > LCM > HPH > EA > AY, and this study establishes a "disruption method to peptide profile to receptor selectivity to flavor quality" framework guiding the industrial production of high-quality YE.

title: A Multimodal Integration Framework for Taste and Odor Prediction and Flavor Molecule Discovery.
abstract: Data-driven molecular property prediction is increasingly used to accelerate molecular discovery and computer-aided design. In flavor science, accurate prediction of molecular taste and odor attributes could facilitate the screening and rational design of candidate flavor molecules. However, this task remains challenging because structure-flavor relationships are complex, single molecular representations may provide incomplete property-relevant information, and the available labels are highly imbalanced. To address these challenges, we implemented and evaluated Uni-Flavor, a multimodal prediction framework embedded in an integrated computational discovery workflow. Uni-Flavor combines three-dimensional molecular representations extracted from a LoRA-fine-tuned Uni-Mol2 model with stability-selected Mordred physicochemical descriptors through a dual-branch fusion architecture incorporating modality-specific projection, multiplicative late fusion, label-aware classification, and imbalance-aware optimization. Independent taste and odor models were trained separately under a common modeling and evaluation protocol, using curated datasets containing 17,202 taste molecules across six categories and 4,983 odor molecules across 138 labels. On held-out test sets, the taste model achieved an accuracy of 95.63% and an AUROC of 97.35%, an AUPRC of 82.05%, and an F1 score of 76.32%, whereas the corresponding values for the odor model were 96.03%, 89.97%, 38.00% and 36.94%. Branch-specific atom-level attribution analysis provided heuristic structural insights into the Uni-Mol2-derived component of the predictions by associating attribution patterns with specific molecular substructures. The trained models were subsequently used to screen approximately 670,000 natural products and coupled with a ScaffoldCAMD strategy for the constrained design of synthetic flavor candidates under chemical-validity, scaffold-assembly, and physicochemical-property constraints, followed by preliminary structural safety filtering. Molecular docking was further used to examine plausible receptor-ligand interactions and provide preliminary receptor-level support for selected candidates. This work presents a common multimodal modeling strategy that integrates three-dimensional molecular representations with physicochemical descriptors and is instantiated independently for multilabel taste and odor prediction. Although developed for flavor-related prediction, evaluation on the SIDER dataset provides preliminary cross-task evidence that the multimodal integration strategy can be applied to another imbalanced multilabel molecular property problem; broader transferability to other property domains remains to be established.

Baking quality attributes were evaluated by measuring specific volume, loaf height, baking loss, color, and texture. Odor activity values (OAVs) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) were used to characterize potential odor-active compounds and differences among treatments. Increasing CRP powder reduced specific volume from 2.98 to 2.54 cm CRP powder substantially reshaped the aroma profile of toast bread but adversely affected loaf expansion and texture at higher addition levels. Overall, 2.0% CRP powder provided a favorable compromise between enhancement of the characteristic CRP aroma and the accompanying changes in baking quality, supporting its potential application as a natural flavoring ingredient in bakery products.

title: Fast and Sensitive Ionogel Capacitive Sensing of Acetic Acid at Room Temperature for Early Plant Salt Stress Detection.
abstract: Acetic acid has been identified as an early biomarker of salt stress in plants, enabling precise monitoring of plant health and timely detection of stress. However, its rapid and selective detection at room temperature remains challenging. Herein, we report an ionogel capacitive chemical sensor based on a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix incorporating the ionic liquid 1-butyl-3-vinylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate ([VBIM][BF4]). The resulting ionogel sensor exhibits high selectivity toward acetic acid over common volatile organic compounds, originating from solvent effects and electrostatic interactions between acetic acid molecules and the ionic liquid, as revealed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Owing to these interactions, the sensor achieves a rapid response time of approximately 6 s at room temperature, and the practical limit of detection is as low as 500 ppb. In addition, the sensor shows excellent long-term stability and mechanical flexibility. The sensor maintains stable sensing performance after 180 days of storage at room temperature and can be integrated with a wireless monitoring system. Furthermore, the sensor detects the acetic acid released by salt-stressed plants, highlighting its potential as an early-warning platform for agricultural stress monitoring.

title: MBWCT-Net: Multiscale Transient Learning for Early Discrimination of Wood-Extracted VOC Mixtures via an Electronic Nose.
abstract: Metal oxide semiconductor electronic noses offer a compact and nondestructive method for volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis. However, reliable recognition of multicomponent mixtures remains challenging because of sensor cross-sensitivity, nonlinear adsorption-desorption dynamics, sensor drift, and long acquisition cycles. Eucalyptus, Rosewood, and Sandalwood essential oils were used as controlled plant-derived VOC benchmarks. Static-headspace gas chromatography-mass spectrometry showed partially shared constituents but distinct dominant headspace fingerprints: Eucalyptus was rich in eucalyptol and monoterpenes, Rosewood was linalool-dominant, and Sandalwood showed a substantially different and partly unresolved profile. The three samples therefore did not exhibit uniformly high compositional similarity. We developed MBWCT-Net, a physics-motivated Multi-Branch Wavelet CNN-Transformer Network that combines a Multi-Scale Wavelet Parallel Network, Lightweight Cross-Attention, and a Multi-Scale Adaptive Transformer to model multiscale response components, cross-band coupling, and local-global temporal dependencies. Under an identical five-fold protocol, MBWCT-Net achieved 95.37 ± 0.61% accuracy and 95.37 ± 0.66% weighted F1, outperforming both raw-input and wavelet-enhanced baselines. Using the first 45 s of the transient response, accuracy reached 94.61 ± 0.70%, within 0.76 percentage points of the complete 60 s response. Deployment on an RK3588 platform yielded a single-sample inference latency of 12.4 ± 0.8 ms and a memory footprint of 48.5 MB. These measurements characterize computational feasibility and do not represent the duration of the complete sensing cycle. Response plots from three independent measurements and normalization-shape checks assessed short-term repeatability and preprocessing effects. Quantitative high-dimensional feature metrics and measured-noise physical-validity analyses evaluated class separability and the preservation of temporal morphology, respectively.

title: Ultrasound-assisted binary probiotic fermentation of sugarcane bagasse dietary fiber-containing synbiotics yogurt: Increased galactitol content to improve yogurt rheological properties and flavor.
abstract: The effect of ultrasound-assisted binary probiotic fermentation on the quality of sugarcane bagasse dietary fiber (SBDF)-added synbiotics yogurt were investigated. The results showed that 0.25 % (w/v) of SBDF significantly reduced yogurt syneresis. Furthermore, ultrasound-assisted fermentation with L. plantarum CGMCC 1.5953 and L. fermentum CGMCC 1.7434 improved the yogurt's texture, rheology, microstructure, and sensory scores. These improvements were supported by metabolomic analysis, which showed an 11.91-fold upregulation of galactitol and decreased concentrations of L-phenylalanine, L-glutamic acid, and L-allothreonine. Integrated sensory and molecular analyses (HS-SPME-GC-MS, UHPLC-MS) identified that enhanced texture scores were associated with SBDF-derived metabolites, including L-erythrulose, α-lactose, and erythritol. Meanwhile, the improved odor scores were associated with increased levels of ethyl acetate, hexanoic acid, and 2-nonanone. Key pathways involve galactose, tyrosine, glycine-serine-threonine metabolism, amino acid biosynthesis, and lysine degradation. This study provides valuable insights for the high-value utilization of sugarcane bagasse dietary fiber and the production of premium-quality yogurt.

title: AI-Enabled Mixed Potential Sensor Array for Complex VOC Mixture Decoding and Real-Time Methanol-Risk Assessment in Baijiu.
abstract: Accurate identification of complex gas mixtures in dynamic real-world environments is essential for environmental monitoring, food safety, and public health. However, these challenges arise mainly from overlapping response fingerprints of chemically similar hazardous analytes and the limited capability of conventional sensors to decouple multicomponent, concentration-coupled signals. Here, we report a ZnFe2O4/MoO3 mixed potential sensor array enabled by a material-device-algorithm co-design strategy. Through compositional engineering of the sensing electrodes, the array generates orthogonal cross-reactive fingerprints for six volatile organic compounds, with response fluctuation standard deviations of 0.47-2.43 mV across all analytes and a rapid response time of 12 s toward 100 ppm triethylamine. To address alcohol mixtures with strong competitive adsorption, including methanol, ethanol, and n-butanol, a CNN-BiLSTM spatiotemporal fusion model extracts multiscale features from dynamic sensing responses, enabling simultaneous mixture classification and concentration prediction. The system achieves recognition accuracies of 100 and 99.33% for the test set and independent validation set, respectively, with corresponding mean absolute errors of 1.61 and 1.62 ppm. We further extend this strategy to a portable Baijiu MeOH sensing platform for real-time methanol-risk assessment in complex liquor matrices, achieving above 98.89% accuracy in identifying samples exceeding the statutory limit. This work integrates interfacial electrochemical regulation, high-dimensional array sensing, deep-learning-enabled signal decoupling, and portable system implementation, offering a deployable route toward intelligent gas sensing in complex real-world environments.

title: Northeastern Chinese Sauerkraut Juice as a Water Replacer in Pork Fillings: Flavor Profiles and Sensory Attributes.
abstract: In this study, the volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles and sensory quality of pork baozi fillings prepared with different substitution levels of Northeastern Chinese sauerkraut juice were characterized using an electronic nose, electronic tongue, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), and gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS). The results showed that both the VOC profiles and sensory attributes of pork baozi fillings varied significantly across sauerkraut juice substitution levels. A total of 80 and 66 VOCs were identified by GC-MS and GC-IMS, respectively. Notably, pork baozi fillings with the 75% sauerkraut juice substitution level exhibited the highest VOC diversity, the highest total VOC content, and the highest overall sensory score. Compared with the control group (12,348.57 μg/kg), the total VOC content increased significantly by 155% to 31,495.61 μg/kg at 75% substitution. Orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) screened out 19 key differential VOCs, including (E,E)-2,4-decadienal, (E)-2-dodecenal, (E)-9-octadecenoic acid ethyl ester, oleic acid and 2,4-hexadienoic acid, ethyl ester. Seventeen fatty acids were quantified, among which (E)-9-octadecenoic acid (C18:1n9t) and palmitic acid (C16:0) accounted for 55.90% and 21.78% of the total fatty acid content, respectively. Partial replacement of water with sauerkraut juice effectively reduced off-flavors in pork baozi fillings and increased the proportion of unsaturated fatty acids, thus improving overall palatability and nutritional quality. This study provides preliminary insights into the flavor modulation mechanism of sauerkraut juice in pork baozi fillings and offers a theoretical basis for the development of high-quality sauerkraut pork products.
authors: Gong D, Wang M, Li C, Liang Z, Zhu D

title: Miniaturized Electronic Noses for Food Quality and Safety: Applications in Lipid Oxidation Monitoring.
abstract: Lipid oxidation is a major degradation process in lipid-rich food systems, producing volatile organic compounds (VOCs) associated with rancidity, off-flavours, and reduced shelf life. Although conventional techniques such as gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) provide reliable identification and quantification of oxidation products, their laboratory-based operation and complex sample preparation limit their suitability for rapid, real-time monitoring. This review examines recent advances in miniaturized and portable electronic-nose (e-nose) systems for monitoring lipid oxidation and food quality through volatile fingerprint analysis. Unlike chromatographic techniques, e-noses generate characteristic response patterns using sensor arrays coupled with pattern recognition and machine learning algorithms rather than directly identifying individual compounds. The relationship between oxidation-derived volatiles, including aldehydes, ketones, alcohols, and hydrocarbons, and e-nose responses are discussed across various food matrices. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors remain the most widely investigated technology because of their robustness, scalability, and portability, while electrochemical, conducting polymer, quartz crystal microbalance (QCM), optical, field-effect transistor (FET), and surface acoustic wave (SAW) sensors are also reviewed. Recent developments in chemometric, machine learning, and deep learning approaches for classification, prediction, and sensor-drift compensation are highlighted, alongside applications in edible oils, meat, dairy products, fermented foods, beverages, coffee, and cocoa. Despite considerable progress, sensor drift, humidity interference, calibration transfer, reproducibility, and limited industrial validations remain important challenges. Future research should prioritize sensor stability, standardized validation protocols, and integration with smart-food-monitoring platforms for reliable real-time quality assessment and shelf-life applications.
authors: Floch M, Gunenc A, Hosseinian F

title: Flavor evolution of Antarctic Krill (Euphausia superba) during thermal processing: insights from GC-IMS, GC-O-MS, and RATA.
abstract: Despite its high nutritional value, the application of Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba, AK) is hindered by complex off-odors. This study integrated electronic nose (E-nose), gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS), and headspace solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-O-MS) with Rate-All-That-Apply (RATA) to map AK flavor evolution under various thermal treatments, including steaming (100 °C for 5 min), frying (220 °C for 5 min), and baking (180 °C for 1 min). Based on the screening criteria of relative odor activity values (ROAV >1), and GC-O detection frequency ≥ 3, 29 key aroma-active compounds were identified. While raw and steamed AK exhibited mild, lipid-derived profiles, frying exacerbated fishy odors due to a surge in lipid oxidation markers (e.g., hexanal, 1-octen-3-ol, and 1-penten-3-one). Conversely, baking optimized the balance of Maillard-lipid interaction profiles, generating sufficient pyrazine-mediated nutty and roasty notes while avoiding excessive lipid oxidation. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) modeling confirmed that baking achieved the highest consumer acceptability, correlated with fruity, meaty, and caramel attributes associated with markers such as trans-2-cis-6-nonadienal, 2-propylfuran, and 5-ethyl-2,3-dimethylpyrazine. These findings provide molecular-level insights for developing sensory-optimized krill products, facilitating the high-value utilization of AK resources.

title: Outer Surface Functionalized Graphene Oxide Nanofluidic Platform for Selective Detection of Insect Pheromones.
abstract: Invasive insects inflict severe ecological and economic damage, creating an urgent need for rapid and early detection strategies. Here, we present a biomimetic strategy that replicates the molecular recognition principles of insect olfaction. As a proof of concept, our platform comprises a graphene oxide membrane with its outer surface functionalized with the pheromone-specific odorant-binding proteins (OBPs) of gypsy moth (Lymantria dispar). The OBP selectively captures the pheromone, (+)-disparlure (DIS), in the vapor phase. This binding event alters the outer surface charge of the nanochannel, which is directly transduced into a measurable change in ionic current─a mechanism that enables vapor-phase molecular recognition using solid-state nanochannels. The sensor detects DIS vapor with exceptional selectivity against nontarget volatiles and a limit of detection of ∼121.7 ppm. It maintains robust performance over 24 days of storage at 4 °C and operates reliably across a wide temperature range (4-60 °C). Crucially, it selectively identifies a single live female gypsy moth within minutes, with no cross-reactivity to other lepidopteran species. By translating the selective mechanism of insect olfaction into a synthetic nanofluidic architecture, this work establishes a versatile and generalizable strategy for proactive pest surveillance in agricultural fields, forests, and border inspection stations.

title: External cavity quantum cascade laser absorption spectroscopy based on convolutional neural network algorithm for volatile organic compounds analysis.
abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are organic compounds having significant impacts on environmental and human health. In this paper, a laser absorption spectroscopy gas sensor system based on an external cavity quantum cascade laser was developed for analyzing multiple VOCs simultaneously. Acetone (C3H6O) and ethanol (C2H6O), as two typical VOCs, were selected as the objects of analysis. Given the overlapping interference issue of C3H6O and C2H6O absorption spectra, a one-dimensional spectral separation convolutional neural network algorithm was developed for VOC spectral signal processing. The experimental results indicated that the spectral fitting residuals were within 0.0028, achieving an 8.77-fold improvement over the traditional partial least squares method. The correlation coefficients for concentration predictions of C3H6O and C2H6O can be improved from 0.9991 and 0.9989 to 0.9996 and 0.9996, respectively, which shows good reliability of the developed algorithm model for both blended absorption spectrum separation and concentration retrieval in the simultaneous detection of multiple gas components.

title: Self-Powered Multivariable Organic Photovoltaic Sensors for Accurate Volatile Organic Compound Discrimination.
abstract: Most existing VOC sensors rely on battery power and only single-parameter outputs, limiting long-term deployment, maintenance efficiency, and chemical discrimination. Here, we report a self-powered multivariable photovoltaic sensor (MPVS) that repurposes an organic photovoltaic junction as an information-rich VOC sensing platform. By integrating a gas-permeable silver nanowire electrode with a donor-acceptor bulk-heterojunction active layer, the MPVS enables efficient analyte access while maintaining stable photovoltaic operation under illumination. Exposure to VOCs induces coupled and reversible changes in open-circuit voltage (VOC) and short-circuit current density (JSC), providing two orthogonal sensing features without external power input. Using a single PM6:Y6 junction, we demonstrate concentration-dependent responses and reliable discrimination of representative VOCs. Extending the concept to a five-element MPVS array incorporating different Y-series acceptors generates high-dimensional photovoltaic fingerprints that enable accurate identification of eight chemically distinct VOCs. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) reveal that analyte-dependent noncovalent interactions, particularly strong hydrogen bonding in the case of formic acid, underlie the observed selectivity. By integrating energy harvesting and multivariate sensing within a single organic photovoltaic platform, this work establishes a scalable, battery-free approach to artificial olfaction, offering a promising pathway for distributed and long-term VOC monitoring systems.

title: Quality divergence of Yunnan upland rice versus Jiangxi and Heilongjiang paddy rice revealed by physicochemical, sensory, volatile and metabolomic profiling.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate quality differences between Yunnan upland rice (YNUR) collected in Honghe, Pu'er, Nujiang and Qujing and paddy rice from Jiangxi and Heilongjiang by physicochemical indexes, taste analyzer, sensory evaluation, e-nose, and untargeted metabolomics. Compared with paddy rice, YNUR exhibited significantly higher amylose content (11.78-14.11%), lower expected glycemic index (60.55-69.13), and higher taste value (8.75-9.01), along with a higher retrogradation value and lower breakdown value. Its texture was characterized by high hardness, high elasticity and low viscosity. Furthermore, YNUR had higher aldehyde and ketone contents, presenting an aroma profile dominated by fruity and faint pungent notes. (Z)-2-nonenal, nonanal and 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine were the key differential odor compounds. Metabolomic analysis identified 573 differential metabolites and revealed significant enrichment of glycerophospholipid and amino acid metabolic pathways in YNUR. This study characterizes the quality attributes of upland rice and provides insights for the cultivation and application of water-saving rice.

title: Proton-Conduction-Mediated High-Performance Ethanol Sensing in a Ni3(HHTP)2/Nafion Composite at Room Temperature.
abstract: Conductive metal-organic frameworks (c-MOFs) are promising chemiresistive sensing materials for selective gas detection; however, their practical deployment is hindered by insufficient selectivity and humidity-induced performance degradation, both of which stem from poorly understood molecular-level conduction mechanisms. Here, we address this gap by engineering a Nafion-functionalized Ni3(HHTP)2 composite that enables a mechanistic shift from electron-dominant to synergistic electron-proton conduction. Through systematic in situ fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR)/X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), we elucidate that the sensing process depends on competitive adsorption between ethanol molecules and prehydrated hydronium ions at the composite interface, disrupting the hydrogen-bond network. The conductive Ni3(HHTP)2 framework ensures efficient electron transport, while Nafion's microphase-separated structure confers dual molecular sieving and preconcentration effects for ethanol. The resulting sensor delivers a high response of 729% to 30 ppm ethanol at RT and 40% RH, exhibits remarkable selectivity, as evidenced by linear discriminant analysis (LDA) with a classification accuracy of 90.91%, and shows rapid kinetics and strong discrimination against common interferents. This work established a fundamental mechanistic framework for proton-electron co-conduction in c-MOFs, supported by in situ spectroscopy and electrochemical analysis. It presents a generalizable interface-modulation strategy for selective volatile organic compound (VOC) sensing under ambient conditions, showing promise for breath analysis applications and industrial safety monitoring.

title: Characterization and decoding of volatile compounds in Rugiboletus extremiorientalis at different drying temperatures: A combined analysis by ATR-FTIR, HS-SPME-GC-MS, E-nose, and molecular docking.
abstract: This study used Attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy, electronic nose, and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) to investigate the composition of Rugiboletus extremiorientalis changes at different drying temperatures. Molecular docking was employed to elucidate the perception mechanism of aroma, and machine learning was utilized to develop a rapid quality evaluation method. The spectral data reflected compositional change patterns, which were validated by GC-MS. As temperature increased, component concentrations and spectral absorbance gradually decreased. 86 potential key aroma compounds were screened based on differential metabolites and relative odor activity values (ROAVs). Binding energy results for these compounds and 15 olfactory receptors (ORs) revealed strong binding affinities, primarily through hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) models based on derivatives and iterative variable subset optimization (IVSO) effectively predicted the content of 25C-8 compounds. This study established a research framework linking compositional changes, the perception mechanisms of flavor molecules, and rapid quality evaluation. This framework provides a theoretical basis for understanding changes in mushroom flavor and molecular perception. It also provides methodological guidance for drying processes and rapid compositional analysis.

title: Differentiable End-to-End Sensor Array Optimization for Electronic Nose via Local Self-Attention.
abstract: Electronic noses (e-noses) based on cross-selective gas sensors often suffer from severe redundancy, which degrades odor analysis accuracy and impedes practical deployment. Here, we introduce a fully deep-learning-based sensor array optimization (SAO) framework that learns an optimal subset of sensor array through an end-to-end differentiable manner. Unlike conventional step-by-step workflows, which separate feature extraction, feature selection, sensor selection, and model training, our method jointly optimizes the sensor selection strategy, feature extractor, and task-specific network, enabling global collaborative optimization. Core to the framework is a local self-attention mechanism that infers sensor-wise importance while preserving the temporal structure of individual sensor responses, together with a tanhshrink-based gating function that drives redundant channels exactly to zero without requiring explicit sparsity regularization. Experiments on a 13-channel polyaniline sensor array exposed to six volatile organic compounds show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 91.18 ± 0.55% using only four sensors, reducing the number of sensors by nearly 70% while outperforming conventional approaches. These results demonstrate that the differentiable SAO can improve both efficiency and accuracy in practical e-nose applications.

title: Liposomal co-delivery of astaxanthin and ascorbic acid: Synergistic regulation of myofibrillar protein interactions and oxidative stability.
abstract: This study systematically investigated the interactions between different liposomes and myofibrillar protein (MP), as well as their effects on the gel structure, water-holding capacity, storage stability, and odor properties of surimi gels. The findings revealed that liposomes, as carrier vehicles, formed stable complexes with MP. These interactions were suggested to be mediated by non-covalent forces, including hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, which induced the transition of the MP secondary structure toward α-helix and a rearrangement of its tertiary structure. An appropriate amount (0.4%) of liposomes significantly improved the water-holding capacity and gel strength of the gels, but excessive addition (0.6%-0.8%) instead caused deterioration of the gel network. Co-encapsulation of astaxanthin and ascorbic acid within liposomes significantly enhanced the antioxidant capacity of the gels through synergistic effects, outperforming the single-loaded liposome group during thermal processing and storage. E-nose analysis indicated that liposome encapsulation reduced the characteristic odor of astaxanthin, as reflected by the overall volatile profile. This study provides a theoretical basis for the development of high-quality functional surimi products.

title: Volatile organic compounds from microalgae: sources, chemical diversity, biosynthesis, and bioactive potential.
abstract: Microalgae are prolific producers of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that play important roles in atmospheric chemistry, aquatic ecosystem dynamics, and water quality, particularly through the generation of off-flavours and odors. Despite their ecological relevance and growing biotechnological interest, microalgal VOCs remain comparatively underexplored. These low-molecular-weight metabolites encompass a broad range of chemical classes, including terpenoids, sulfur-containing compounds, benzenes, furans, alkanes, alcohols, ketones, aldehydes, and esters. Knowledge of their chemical diversity, biosynthetic pathways, allelopathic effects, and other ecological functions is still not fully reviewed. This review synthesizes current understanding of microalgal VOCs, emphasizing how morphology, physiology, ecological niche, and genetic variability influence VOCs production. Commonly reported VOCs such as geosmin, methylisoborneol, β-cyclocitral, and 2-pentylfuran are discussed with respect to their occurrence, chemistry, ecological roles, regulation by biotic and abiotic factors, and impacts. Despite their diverse ecological and biochemical roles, limited elucidation of their biosynthetic mechanisms also highlighted. Microalgal VOCs exhibit diverse bioactivities, including antibacterial, antifungal, insecticidal, antioxidant, antiviral, and antiprotozoal properties, underscoring their potential for biotechnological and industrial applications. Advances in analytical approaches, particularly gas chromatography-mass spectrometry and electronic nose technologies, have significantly improved VOCs detection and profiling. This review identifies critical knowledge gaps and underscores the need for integrative studies to unravel the diversity, chemical structures, biosynthetic pathways, and ecological significance of microalgal VOCs, thereby enabling theirsustainable exploitation and facilitating their industrial applications.

title: An Artificial Olfactory Chip with Temperature Gradient Modulation for Food Waste Management.
abstract: Increasing demand for fuels driven by the scarcity of fossil resources necessitates the development of sustainable and innovative strategies for the energy industry. Food waste has emerged as a viable resource with diverse functional chemical components for energy harvesting. To enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of energy generation from food waste, classification and monitoring of food waste are crucial. Traditional vision recognition methods often face challenges due to waste overlaps and environmental constraints. In contrast, employing artificial olfactory chips (AOCs) holds promise in classifying food waste via gaseous information. However, bulky size, low sensitivity, limited classification ability, poor robustness, and lack of scalability hinder the implementation of AOCs into food waste management systems. Herein, we report a compact, monolithic AOC featuring a gas sensor array with temperature gradient modulation (TGM-Array), offering a promising platform for this application. Constructed on a porous anodized aluminum oxide (AAO) template with a high surface area, the TGM-Array chips demonstrate high sensitivity, detecting ethanol (EtOH) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) at concentrations as low as 100 parts-per-billion (ppb). Leveraging the response patterns from sensing pixels at different operating temperatures, the TGM-Array chips exhibit effective discriminability. They categorized EtOH and H2S by type and concentration and distinguished selected food waste samples, such as beef and tomatoes, as well as their mixtures at different post-disposal durations under controlled experimental conditions. In addition, the TGM-Array chips maintain good robustness across four testing periods, identifying beef and tomato samples with varied post-disposal durations. Furthermore, their fabrication processes are photolithography-free and involve only three steps, rendering the TGM-Array chips cost-effective and well-suited for large-scale deployment in trash bins. These capabilities suggest the potential of TGM-Array chips for developing intelligent trash bin systems for improving food waste management efficiency and enhancing energy recovery processes.

title: Elevated expression of olfactory receptor 51T1 is associated with malignant potential of bladder cancer.
abstract: The olfactory receptor gene (OR) superfamily is the largest in the human genome. ORs are expressed not only in the neurons of the olfactory epithelium but also in various other tissues in which their functions are largely unknown. We investigated the association between OR51T1 expression in bladder cancer and its malignant potential. We immunohistochemically examined the expression of OR51T1 in a set of tissue microarray consisting of bladder cancer specimens from 154 patients. We also assessed the effect of OR51T1 silencing via siRNA transfection on the viability of bladder cancer cells. Low levels of OR51T1 expression were detected in 93 (60.4%) bladder cancer cases, whereas 61 (39.6%) showed high levels of OR51T1 expression. OR51T1 expression was significantly elevated in higher grade tumors (p < 0.001). However, there were no significant associations of OR51T1 expression with other clinicopathological features, such as sex, age, and pathological T stage. In a bladder cancer cell line, OR51T1 silencing resulted in significant inhibition in cell proliferation. OR51T1 expression in bladder cancer was found to be associated with higher grade or cell proliferation. These findings suggest the involvement of OR51T1 in bladder cancer progression.

title: In situ hybridization analysis of the expression of class I and II odorant receptors in the olfactory organ of the African spurred tortoise (Centrochelys sulcata).
abstract: The olfactory organ of turtles consists of an upper chamber epithelium (UCE) associated with glands and a lower chamber epithelium (LCE) lacking glands. The odorant receptors (ORs) are a family of olfactory receptors generally categorized into classes I and II based on sequence similarity. In amniotes, class I and II ORs are thought to preferentially detect hydrophilic and hydrophobic molecules, respectively. The relative abundance of OR classes vary among turtles: while class I ORs predominate in aquatic turtles, class II ORs are more abundant in terrestrial turtles. However, it remains unclear where these receptors are expressed in the olfactory organ of turtles. In this study, we identified eight class I ORs and 61 class II ORs and examined the distribution of OR-expressing cells in the olfactory organ of the African spurred tortoise (Centrochelys sulcata). In situ hybridization analysis revealed that all representative class I ORs examined in C. sulcata are expressed in both the UCE and the LCE, whereas all representative class II ORs examined are restricted to the UCE. These findings are in marked contrast to our previous observations in the olfactory organ of the sea turtle Chelonia mydas. Also, double-labeling experiments revealed that class I ORs are not co-expressed with the transcription factor B-cell lymphoma/leukemia 11b (Bcl11b), suggesting that Bcl11b-mediated repression of class I OR expression is conserved in C. sulcata. Present findings suggest that ecological adaptation of turtles may be correlated with variation in the expression site of ORs within the olfactory organ.

title: Advanced insights into the adsorption mechanism of coumarin compounds on mouse olfactory receptors: a statistical physics, thermodynamic, and molecular docking analysis.
abstract: In this paper, a combined statistical physics and computational modeling framework was used to elucidate the molecular mechanism of olfaction through a putative adsorption process in which coumarin compounds bind to the mouse olfactory receptors Olfr924, Olfr285, and Olfr1016. Adsorption isotherms derived from experimental data were analyzed using both monolayer and double-layer statistical physics models, enabling the quantitative determination of steric and energetic parameters governing odorant-receptor interactions. The steric analysis reveals diverse anchoring behaviors, with coumarin molecules adopting both parallel and non-parallel orientations relative to receptor binding sites, indicative of mixed adsorption configurations. The estimated adsorption energies, ranging from 13.563 to 33.872 kJ/mol, suggest that the coumarin compounds are physically adsorbed onto the receptors, offering insight into the steric and energetic heterogeneity of the receptor. Moreover, the application of statistical physics modeling enabled a detailed steric characterization of the receptor surface through binding site size distributions (BSDs) and an energetic characterization via adsorption energy distributions (AEDs). To complement microscopic analysis, a macroscopic thermodynamic study was also performed, providing further insight into the adsorption behavior of coumarin compounds on the olfactory receptors. To further validate and complement these findings, molecular docking simulations were performed to identify interaction types and binding modes between coumarin ligands and olfactory receptors. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating statistical physics modeling with molecular docking to elucidate mechanisms of olfactory perception at both microscopic and macroscopic scales. The three complexes formed between coumarin and the olfactory receptor sites (Olfr285, Olfr924, and Olfr1016) have been analyzed using molecular docking simulations, molecular dynamics simulations, and free binding energies calculated using the molecular mechanics-Poisson-Boltzmann surface (MM-PBSA) and molecular mechanics-generalized Born surface (MM-GBSA) methods.

title: Cooperation between Adh and OR5M11 contributes to the lung pathogenicity of Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae by facilitating the NLRP3-mediated inflammatory response.
abstract: Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae (A. pleuropneumoniae) is the etiologic agent of porcine pleuropneumonia, a severe respiratory disease characterized by hemorrhagic, necrotizing lung lesions that cause significant economic losses on the global swine industry. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the lung pathogenicity of A. pleuropneumoniae remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that A. pleuropneumoniae infection induces lung injury through activating the NLRP3-mediated inflammatory response mediated by the YadA-like head region (Adh) of Apa1, a bacterial adhesin that mediates attachment to host cells. Importantly, we show that Adh triggers the NLRP3-mediated inflammatory response by engaging olfactory receptor family 5 subfamily M member 11 (OR5M11), a host receptor previously shown to interact with Adh. Furthermore, OR5M11 contributes to the Adh-activated inflammatory response by promoting mitochondrial DNA release. Taken together, our results provide new insights into the pathogenesis of A. pleuropneumoniae, particularly regarding NLRP3-mediated inflammatory pathology.

title: Exhaled breath metabolomics: Clinical diagnostic applications, technological evolution and translational challenges.
abstract: Breathomics, the analysis of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and other metabolites in exhaled breath, offers a non-invasive approach to disease screening, longitudinal monitoring and assessment of treatment response. Advances in gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, real-time mass spectrometry, electronic-nose (e-nose) sensors and machine-learning workflows have markedly improved the sensitivity and diagnostic performance of breath analysis. However, these gains have been demonstrated mainly in proof-of-concept and analytical validation studies, and remain insufficiently confirmed in prospective clinical cohorts. In this Review, we examine breathomics across the translational pathway, from breath sampling and pre-analytical standardization to analytical platforms, data processing, disease applications and clinical implementation. We focus on three clinically prominent areas, cancer, chronic respiratory disease and infectious disease, and use selected systemic disorders to illustrate the limited disease specificity of individual VOCs. Current evidence supports the presence of detectable disease-associated breath signatures, but most VOC panels remain insufficiently standardized, externally validated and mechanistically interpretable for routine clinical use. Translation will require harmonized sampling protocols, rigorous analytical validation, prospective multicenter cohorts, explainable models, regulatory approval, and evidence of clinical utility and cost-effectiveness.

title: The functional diversification of somatosensory neuron repertoires across Mammalia.
abstract: The striking diversity of mammalian body forms and surfaces, lifestyles, and habitats prompts the question of how each species' somatosensory neuron repertoire accommodates such diversity. The visual and olfactory systems diversify by gaining and losing sensor/receptor genes and corresponding sensory cell types. Using multiomic single-cell analysis of dorsal root ganglia neurons from thirteen different mammalian species and cross-species functional studies enabled by cell-type-specific enhancer viruses, we show that mammals instead assemble species-specific, functionally distinct somatosensory neuron repertoires from a conserved set of neuron types (orthotypes). Repertoire diversification takes multiple forms: orthotype abundance scales with variable bodily traits like hair follicle density, facilitating relevant behaviors; sensor/receptor expression is shuffled across species, such that orthotypes can detect different stimuli in different species; and orthotypes split into functionally distinct, species-specific subtypes (paratypes). Thus, unlike other sensory systems, the mammalian somatosensory system diversifies through multifarious changes to conserved orthotypes, enabling adaptation to diverse habitats, lifestyles, and body forms.

title: Graphene-Enabled Breathomics: A Translational Roadmap from Fundamental Physics to Non-Invasive Point-of-Care Diagnostics.
abstract: Selective molecular recognition of trace volatile biomarkers in humid breath remains a fundamental coordination challenge at graphene interfaces. While exhaled breath contains a complex matrix of more than 3500 volatile organic compounds, clinical transition has been largely challenged by the selectivity-humidity paradox. This review traces the evolution of graphene transduction platforms from fundamental quantum phenomena to coordination-governed interfacial engineering strategies enabling selective molecular recognition. It critically analyzes the atomic-level interactions governing the interface, specifically how sublattice symmetry breaking, metal-ligand interactions, competitive water coordination, and 1/f noise spectroscopy enable detection limits at the parts-per-trillion level. It details nanoengineering strategies for superior performance, tracing the shift from pristine graphene to 2D/2D heterostructures and organic-functionalized scaffolds that introduce defined coordination environments to regulate analyte binding and suppress humidity interference. These coordination-engineered platforms are linked with clinical targets such as oncology and metabolic disorders, while machine intelligence serves as a supporting analytical layer within the sensor intelligence paradigm. Crucially, it addresses the path to clinical translation, emphasizing first-in-human safety milestones, green synthesis, and economic scalability afforded by adopting laser-induced graphene. By unifying 2D-material physics, coordination-driven selectivity, and sensor intelligence, graphene breathomics provides a chemically grounded framework for decentralized, personalized diagnostic technologies.

title: Classification of Volatile Organic Compounds Using a Novel High-Frequency Quartz Crystal Microbalance Sensor Array Based on Ethyl Cellulose Microstructures.
abstract: Detecting volatile organic compounds (VOCs) is essential because they affect air quality and can serve as biomarkers for non-invasive early disease detection. VOCs can be identified using electronic noses combining cross-reactive sensors, pattern recognition, and classification algorithms. Here, a single-polymer 12-sensor array based on 30 MHz quartz crystal microbalances was developed using three ethyl cellulose (EC) microstructures: casting films (CFs), anti-solvent microparticles (ASMs), and electrospray microparticles (ESMs). The array detected ethanol, ethyl acetate, and heptane at ppm concentrations under controlled conditions of 20 °C and 20% relative humidity. Scanning electron micrographs exhibited average mesh-hole diameters of 1.13 ± 0.44 μm for CFs, and average particle diameters of 60 ± 15 nm and 1.1 ± 0.3 μm for ASMs and ESMs, respectively. FTIR spectra indicated O-H and H-O-H bending bands for ASMs and EC, whereas these bands were notably attenuated for ESMs, suggesting their affinities for polar and non-polar compounds, respectively. Mahalanobis distance and a support vector machine classifier accurately discriminated VOCs in principal component analysis space. Principal component regression and partial least squares regression predicted VOC concentrations with R2 > 0.99, achieving estimated limits of detection of 143.6, 57, and 42.1 ppm by PCR and 70.5, 32.8, and 26.5 ppm by PLSR for ethanol, ethyl acetate, and heptane, respectively.

title: An NB-IoT-Based Architecture with Spatial-Statistical Analytics for Cross-Domain Air and Water Quality Monitoring in Aquaculture and Aquatic Environments.
abstract: The rapid expansion of smart agriculture and precision aquaculture necessitates continuous, high-resolution environmental monitoring to optimize ecosystem stability and prevent catastrophic biomass loss. Conventional Internet of Things (IoT) solutions routinely treat atmospheric and aquatic parameters as isolated domains, neglecting the dynamic physicochemical coupling occurring across the air-water boundary layer. To overcome this domain fragmentation, this study presents an integrated edge-cloud telemetry architecture designed for concurrent, multi-domain environmental monitoring and cross-domain spatial-statistical analysis. The proposed framework employs low-cost, multi-sensor edge nodes integrated with Narrowband IoT (NB-IoT) cellular communication, achieving high signal penetration, energy-efficient operation, and direct base-station connectivity without local gateway dependencies. The system continuously acquires atmospheric parameters (temperature, relative humidity, particulate matter PM1.0/PM2.5/PM10, ozone O3, total volatile organic compounds TVOC, equivalent CO2, Air Quality Index AQI, and Ultraviolet Index UVI) alongside aquatic indicators (water temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen DO, electrical conductivity EC, and turbidity). Telemetry is streamed via Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to a centralized MySQL cloud database, providing real-time Grafana dashboards, spatial Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) mapping, and automated multi-channel alerting via LINE Notify and email. title: Multi-Scale Temporal-Dependency Learning for Single-Sensor Gas Classification.
abstract: Single-sensor gas classification remains challenging because metal oxide semiconductor sensors exhibit limited selectivity and different gases can produce similar response patterns. This paper proposes a multi-scale temporal-dependency-learning framework that combines reservoir-based multi-scale dynamic learning (MsDL) with lagged-correlation features. To reduce information leakage caused by window construction, each continuous gas-response sequence is divided chronologically into training, validation, and test blocks before window extraction, and 2000 raw samples are excluded between adjacent subsets. The primary evaluation uses non-overlapping windows and fits all data-dependent preprocessing using the training subset only. On a dataset containing seven volatile organic compounds measured using a single sensor, the proposed MsDL+Corr representation with a random-forest classifier achieves a test accuracy of 92.14% and a macro-F1 score of 92.08%. Across ten random-forest seeds, the accuracy is 92.43% ± 0.37%. The corresponding micro-average one-vs-rest AUC is 0.9948 (99.48%); this threshold-independent ranking metric is distinct from classification accuracy. Feature ablation shows that combining MsDL and correlation features improves the macro-F1 score over either branch alone. These results demonstrate that temporal-dependency representations provide useful discriminative information under a conservative temporally separated evaluation protocol.

title: Genome-wide analyses of olfactory receptor repertoires in Glyptosternon maculatum: Implications for evolutionary dynamics and high-altitude adaptation.
abstract: The evolutionary dynamics of the olfactory receptor (OR) gene family are key to fish adaptation across diverse ecological niches. However, the mechanisms associated with olfactory adaptation to high-altitude environments remain poorly understood. As the Sisoridae species with the highest altitudinal distribution, Glyptosternon maculatum serves as an ideal model for investigating the genetic mechanisms of such adaptation. We conducted genome-wide identification and comparative analysis of OR genes in G. maculatum and 11 other Siluriformes species. The results revealed that G. maculatum harbored 74 OR genes, comprising 65 functional genes, 7 pseudogenes, and 2 partial genes. It possessed the lowest number of OR genes and functional OR genes among the 12 species, and the highest proportion of pseudogenes. Further comparative analysis showed that G. maculatum had only four OR gene families (δ, η, λ, ζ) and 52 subfamilies, with no species-specific subfamilies identified. Selection pressure analysis showed that all calculated Ka/Ks ratios for OR genes in G. maculatum were less than 1 when compared with Bagarius rutilus (same family) and Ictalurus punctatus (same order, different family). Additionally, no significant differences were observed in the physicochemical properties of functional OR proteins among the 12 fish species. Sequence analysis of conserved motifs in OR genes revealed that the conserved motifs across the 12 Siluriformes species shared similar sequence compositions. These results indicated that the OR gene repertoire of G. maculatum exhibits distinctive evolutionary characteristics that may be associated with its high-altitude habitat. Our findings may provide a foundation for understanding potential olfactory adaptation to high-altitude environments in G. maculatum.

title: Characterization and postprandial regulation of the nutrient-sensing machinery in the oral floor mucosa of 10-week-old mule ducks.
abstract: In birds, oral nutrient detection contributes to regulating ingestive behavior, yet the molecular repertoire and postprandial dynamics of gustatory pathways remain poorly defined in ten-week-old ducks. This study evaluated the postprandial responses of nutrient-sensing receptors, calcium-signaling components, and monoaminergic pathways in the oral floor mucosa and central neural tissue of ten-week-old mule ducks. Fed and fasted ducks were sampled at 0 min, 20 min, 2 h, 6 h, and 12 h following meal distribution. Transcriptional profiling revealed a broad chemosensory repertoire spanning sweet, umami, bitter, sour, and fatty acid modalities in the oral floor mucosa, supporting its role as a key sensory interface. However, most gustatory and calcium-signaling genes exhibited remarkable transcriptional stability postprandially at this developmental stage. Notably, only the lipid sensor CD36 (Cluster of differentiation 36) and the bitter receptor T2R116 (Taste receptor type 2 member 116) displayed a significant time × feeding interaction, indicating targeted peripheral responsiveness for fat and bitter perception. Conversely, postprandial changes were marked in monoaminergic circuits. Serotonin metabolism in the oral floor mucosa varied by nutritional state during the early postprandial phase, while elevated central serotonin concentrations and enhanced dopaminergic turnover in fed ducks evidenced acute activation of central satiety and reward circuits. Concurrently, hypothalamic gene expression revealed a synchronized time-dependent downregulation of POMC (Proopiomelanocortin) and MC4R (Melanocortin 4 receptor) up to 6 h post-feeding. In parallel, plasma chemerin levels increased postprandially, highlighting a coordinated peripheral metabolic response. Overall, these results indicate that short-term postprandial regulation in ten-week-old ducks relies predominantly on rapid neurochemical adjustments rather than transcriptional remodeling of peripheral gustatory receptors.
